The *Utena Sutta* (Ud 7.10; PTS Ud 79) is the concluding discourse of the seventh chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative centers on an incident in which five hundred awakened women die in a fire [SuttaCentral]. Within later canonical and paracanonical exegesis, the sutta is referenced in the *Paññattihāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 14) [SuttaCentral].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial Pali-internal text reuse, sharing 92 passages with 28 other canonical and commentarial works [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlaps are found in the *Kosala Saṁyutta* (SN 3, where §2.1–2.4 aligns closely with SN 3.9) and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (matching §2.2–5.6) [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic segments are also shared with the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Sundarī Sutta* (Ud 4.8), the *Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta* (SN 5), and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any extant cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
